results.title: Holy Sadhu !
results.text: Those holy men have a great business taking photo money from the tourists. Alas, I was guilty once of paying them to get some brilliant photos. The site is a must see though on cremation days it is not everyones cup of tea. You can not enter the Hindy temple (hindu only).

results.title: Most sacred Hindu temple
results.text:
We came to visit around sundown, when the temple was opened for Hindu (only) pilgrims. It was fascinating to watch and a local guide explained us the site. Consider taking a guide, especially if you are unfamiliar with Hinduism. The Puja ritual (singing and music) in the evening was wonderful and people sing and dance along with it. Definitely try to watch that (it is on the other side of the temple).
The ghats, where Hindus are cremated within 24 hours of death, are down by the river. Take your time if you are hesitant about watching such a funeral. They take place 24/7. First, the deceased gets washed on the northern side of the bridge. Then the cremation is done on the ghats. For me personally, it was fascinating to watch the funeral ritual.

results.title: very unusual
results.text:
you can see on one side of the river people eating and splashing in a water and in a few meters, next side washing of a dead body and preparation for cremation. I was a bit shocked standing in few meters away from cremating body, ash of cremating fire was falling on my hair and listening the story of castes...
Shocking but very interesting place. 
Good chance to think about life and death and some other philosophical issues.
the guide who join you upon your arrival will extort money.

results.title: Must if you haven't been to Varanasi
results.text:
This temple is the holiest Hindu temple in KTM. It is very big, I mean the whole complex is spread across the both banks of the Baghmati river. The temple itself is not accessible to non Hindu and architecturally is nothing special.
I see everybody is talking about cremation. Two days before KTM we were in Varanasi, and compared to those cremations in Varanasi, those at Pashupatinath are far less impressive. Besides, it was too much for our stomachs to watch those sad scenes again.
The people, pilgrims and locals at the temple, we found far more interesting. But beware of them. Half of them are not real holy men and pilgrims. They are dressed in such a way to take photos with them and then ask for money.

results.title: Green and park like
results.text:
A local Nepali friend took me here, and it was a lovely glance into Hindu culture amidst wonderful architecture and gardens.  The monkeys and deer were fun too.  Walk up and down to get to the sacred river to see the cremations waiting to happen.  It does cost 1000 NPR for
foreigners to enter.  Could easily spend a couple of hours enjoying this holy site honoring Shiva and other central Hindu gods and goddesses.

results.title: Truly divine!
results.text: The feel about the place brings out the spiritual side of yours. I witnessed the evening aarti.. amazing experience. Must visit.

results.title: Hindu Cremation Site
results.text: I will never forget my visit to this Hindu temple since I personally witnessed the cremation of bodies. You will also hear the wailing of relatives crying before their relatives and loved ones are cremated. Its interesting to see bodies in a pyre of wood and some of them being place near the river where young boys jump and swim. There are a lot of interesting buildings ,events and people to see in this Hindu temple specially Hindus who cover their bodies and faces with colored dye.

results.title: dream fulfilled
results.text:
filled with mostly local public. but a very different kind of temple compared to indian temple.
the tradito is also different. memeorable experience in visiting the shiv linga.

results.title: The Holy Way
results.text: Pashupatinath is considered as the holiest Hindu Pilgrimage and as me being from Kathmandu I have been there countless times. Nowadays it has become very clean compared to olden days and which is praiseworthy. A must visit for all the Hindus who go to Kathmandu.

results.title: Another approach of mourning
results.text: This place is a must-see, though it can be very dismal and/or depressing. On the shores of the narrow Bagmati River locals cremate their deceased on 24/7. The main temple is for Hindus only, but the site altogether is a very impressive sight. Try not to run through this; it is time to meditate on life and death there.

results.title: Temple with great value
results.text: It is regarded as one of the famous temple for hindu people. Has great art and architecture and moreover, the belief of the hindu people towards the lord Shiva is appreciable. Full of architecture and ancient art.

results.title: i have Faith.
results.text: Pashupatinath is a deity and much revered by thousands of pilgrims who come here everyday. The legends go back thousands of years. But the modern day control and highhandedness of the priests in charge disturbs me.

results.title: Nice temple ..
results.text:
Liked the temple, the sheer size and the rituals going on is worth a visit.

However non Hindus are not allowed into the main temple. And there is a fee to enter the temple.

results.title: Amazing
results.text: As a western Christian its not every day I see people cremated in the open and then dumped into the river.  Amazing to see how they celebrate the end of life.  Great area to walk around and explore.  Get a guide if you want to learn the history.

results.title: Most popular Hindu destination!!
results.text: Pashupatinath temple is the major destination of Hindus all around the world. It is one of the most significant temples of lord shiva. It's religious values and history have earned its place in unesco world heritage sites. Artistic excellence of wood carving can be observed in various parts of this temple. It is situated on the bank of bagmati river.

results.title: DIVINE EXPERIENCE !!!
results.text: First of all !! to let you this.. this temple is only meant for Hindus and yes most of the times being a non Hindu you are prohibited to enter .. now once you are inside the temple.. trust me you can actually feel a strange energy surrounding you .. yes you will experience it.. an very ancient and an amazing construction will not stop you from gazing at the beautiful wooden carvings at the top of the temple. extremely sacred place .. also you have many temples in the same compound of this temple one being a kaal bhairav temple..must see.. at the back of the temple you have many other small temples full of sadhus.. mind you !! most of these sadhus are fake and they are there to make money by clicking photographs with the visitors.. a small bridge goes over the river and yes you have got a lot of hindu last rituals being performed there with ashes being submerged in the river..now i suggest you to cross a bridge going over the river and enter a small forest ..and go upto the top and descend down to one of the sacred hindu shakti-peets of ghuheswari!! dont miss this.. in all an amazing and divine experience !!

results.title: Thought provoking
results.text: Although we weren't sure about visiting this because of the cremations and left it until our last day, it was a moving experience. Traveling to the other side of the world, one needs to open up to things that might make you squeamish at home. Seeing the open-air cremations is only a small part of visiting this huge complex of temples. We took a guide who explained the meaning of a lot of the rites, as well as the details of the different temples. Meeting and being blessed by the sadhus was a humbling moment and seeing the caves and simple housing they lived in precariously perched on the mountainside, showed the depth of their devotion. Is was a privilege to be allowed to observe tis holy place.

results.title: Pashupatinath Temple
results.text:
Very interesting old area.
But watch out for the professional holy men,they're very expensive.
Otherwise its interesting just to walk around by yourself and pick up on the atmosphere.
Tends to gets smoky around dusk.

results.title: Could be much better
results.text: People here do not mKe you feel very welcome: the temple is off limit for non hindus and the place is not kept clean. Too many tounts too

results.title: Absolutely amazing!
results.text: I don't think I have encountered an experience such as Pasupathinath Temple before. Thankfully we hired a guide at the entrance to the temple. Best travel I advice I can give you. We might have just walked up to the rivers edge to view the first few funeral pyres on the other side and then left. Fortunately our guide took us all around the entire complex, with the climax being the section of the temple where the bodies wrapped in orange cloth were lying along the river waiting to be burned. The view from up high from the opposite bank of the river of the entire ritual will stay with me forever.
